title: Acute mesenteric ischaemia - evaluation of an interdisciplinary treatment concept based on a retrospective cohort study
summary: Acute mesenteric ischaemia (AMI) is a life-threatening condition. It is caused by a sudden interruption of the blood supply to the intestine. Without treatment, it can lead to intestinal necrosis, peritonitis, multiple organ failure and death (Tilsed et al., 2016).  AMI is difficult to diagnose as the symptoms are not clear. Between 50 % and 80 % of those affected die, especially if the diagnosis is delayed (Kärkkäinen & Acosta, 2017). This study evaluates the introduction of a standard operating procedure (SOP) for AMI therapy.

interventions.name: This retrospective study evaluates the introduction of a standard operating procedure (SOP) for AMI therapy. The primary endpoint of this study is hospital mortality.
